name: Rhino Linux
summary: An Ubuntu-based rolling-release distribution built upon the Ubuntu development branch, featuring snapshot release 2026.1, the Pacstall package manager, the unified rhino-pkg CLI, and the custom XFCE-based Unicorn Desktop.

content.introduction: Rhino Linux is a community-driven GNU/Linux distribution that re-invents the Ubuntu operating system as a continuous, rolling-release desktop platform. Co-founded in 2023 by AJ Allen and Oren Klopfer, the project diverges from traditional Ubuntu interim and LTS cycles. By coupling Ubuntu's development branch (`devel`) with Pacstall—an AUR-inspired package manager for Debian/Ubuntu systems—and the custom-built Unicorn Desktop, Rhino Linux delivers rapid upstream updates within a stable, lightweight XFCE framework.
content.what_is_it: Technically, Rhino Linux is a rolling-release operating system tracking the continuous `devel` branch of Ubuntu repositories. It unifies package management through `rhino-pkg` (RPK / RPK2 written in Nushell), a master command-line tool that aggregates Pacstall, APT, Flatpak, and Snap. The desktop environment is powered by the custom 'Unicorn Desktop', which combines an XFCE baseline with modern application grids, the Plank dock, and custom utility scripts.
content.origin_and_history: Rhino Linux originated in 2020 from the 'Rolling Rhino' script created by Martin Wimpress, designed to track Ubuntu's development repositories. Developer AJ Allen subsequently launched 'Rolling Rhino Remix' to turn the script into installable disk images. Recognizing architectural limitations in the initial remix, the team executed a complete rebuild in early 2023, establishing Rhino Linux as an independent distribution. The project showcased its technical milestones at FOSDEM 2025, delivering regular snapshot releases including 2025.1 and 2026.1.
content.ubuntu_devel_and_rolling_model: Unlike traditional Ubuntu releases that require point-release upgrades every six months or two years, Rhino Linux treats Ubuntu's development archive as a perpetual rolling release. Users install the system once and receive continuous software updates, eliminating the disruptive system upgrades and PPA breakages that often accompany major distribution version migrations.
content.pacstall_and_aur_concept: A core architectural pillar of Rhino Linux is `Pacstall`, an independent package manager built specifically to function like Arch Linux's AUR for Ubuntu-based systems. Pacstall allows users and developers to build, package, and install software directly from upstream source repositories or GitHub releases using straightforward `pacscript` recipes. This mechanism supplies Rhino Linux with the newest Linux kernels, developer tools, and desktop applications before they enter Debian or Ubuntu archives.
content.rhino_pkg_unified_management: To eliminate the friction of managing multiple package managers, Rhino Linux provides `rhino-pkg` (invoked via `rpk`). Rewritten in Nushell for speed and structured data handling (RPK2), `rhino-pkg` serves as a unified command-line wrapper. A single syntax allows users to update the entire operating system across APT, Pacstall, Flatpaks, and Snaps simultaneously (`rpk update`), or search across all four repository ecosystems in a single command.
content.unicorn_desktop_experience:
The default user interface of Rhino Linux is the 'Unicorn Desktop'. Engineered on top of XFCE to maintain low RAM and CPU consumption, Unicorn modernizes the user experience by integrating:

- Plank: A clean, animated application dock for fast multitasking.
- App Grid & Ulauncher: Rapid keyboard-driven application launching and system navigation.
- Custom Theming & Unicons: Unified modern icon sets, dark mode styling, and consistent window borders.
- Dynamic Workspaces: Fluid virtual desktop management adapted for modern widescreen displays.
content.hardware_support_and_arm64: Rhino Linux supports both standard 64-bit x86_64 PCs and ARM64 (`aarch64`) architectures. Dedicated disk images are produced for ARM single-board computers including Raspberry Pi and Pine64 devices (PinePhone, Pinebook Pro). System deployment on desktop PCs is handled by the Calamares installer, followed by the `rhino-setup` wizard to configure initial user preferences.
content.release_artifacts_and_platform_images: Rhino Linux 2026.1 is published as a generic x86_64 image of 2.70 GiB and a generic ARM64 image of 2.69 GiB, both shipping the Unicorn desktop and the 7.0.9-generic kernel. Dedicated ARM64 builds are provided for PINE64 devices and for the Raspberry Pi, and every image is published with a sha256 checksum. Earlier releases are archived on SourceForge, container images are published separately, and the source code is linked from the download page.
content.installation_and_conversion_paths: The wiki splits its user documentation along the installation paths it supports: a general installation guide, a page for the ISO and live image, one page for PINE64 devices and one for the Raspberry Pi, followed by post-installation steps. Two further chapters cover adopting the system on hardware that already runs something else - switching an installation to UBXI and converting an existing system to Rhino Linux - and a separate chapter documents Nvidia driver installation. The same wiki explains the rolling model as one in which no major upgrade step exists, packages being updated continuously instead.
content.hotfix_mechanism_and_patch_distribution: The security-relevant machinery documented by the project is a hotfix channel rather than a published disclosure policy. `rhino-hotfix` is a command-line utility whose stated purpose is to distribute and apply hotfixes and patches to existing installations. It takes the name of a hotfix and can be pointed at a specific source through a metalink argument that selects a repository, a branch, or a pull request, for example `rhino-hotfix hotfix@#42` to fetch a candidate from pull request 42, or `rhino-hotfix` with no argument to list the available hotfixes from the project repository. Ordinary software updates travel through Pacstall and APT, so security fixes reach installed systems through the rolling update stream. The public wiki indexes no vulnerability disclosure page and no advisory archive; the hotfix utility and the rolling repository are therefore the documented mechanisms, and the absence of a formal disclosure policy is a limit of the project's public documentation rather than a property established here.
advantages: True rolling-release model for Ubuntu eliminating disruptive point-release upgrades
Native Pacstall integration providing an AUR-like repository for the newest upstream software
Unified rhino-pkg CLI managing APT, Pacstall, Flatpak, and Snap in a single command
Lightweight Unicorn Desktop based on XFCE delivering high responsiveness and low resource usage
Official support for both 64-bit x86 PCs and ARM64 single-board computers like Raspberry Pi
Modern Calamares installer with post-installation setup wizard
disadvantages: Tracking the Ubuntu devel branch can occasionally introduce upstream packaging regressions
Smaller maintainer team compared to major enterprise-backed rolling distributions
Pacstall package catalog is smaller than the comprehensive Arch User Repository (AUR)
Unicorn Desktop is currently based on X11, with full Wayland transition still under development
who_is_it_for: Ubuntu and Debian enthusiasts who desire continuous rolling package updates without reinstallations
Developers needing an AUR-style source build system (Pacstall) within an APT-compatible environment
Users seeking a modern, dock-centric desktop interface with the lightweight efficiency of XFCE
ARM64 experimenters running modern Linux on Raspberry Pi or Pine64 single-board computers
who_is_it_not_for: Enterprise server environments requiring multi-year LTS package stability and enterprise support SLAs
Users who want a pure upstream GNOME or KDE Plasma desktop without customized wrapper environments
Novice users uncomfortable with resolving occasional package dependency adjustments in a rolling distribution
content.verdict: Rhino Linux is a rolling-release distribution built on Ubuntu. Powered by Pacstall, the rhino-pkg wrapper, and the Unicorn Desktop, it provides a continuously updated Ubuntu-based system.
